clue.text: Favourably placed tenor spoke of missing mass with the best of motives

parts.note: someone well in with others is in a favoured position
T is the standard abbreviation for tenor in music

indicators.note: missing tells us a letter is dropped from the word for 'spoke of'

parts.note: to speak of something is to mention it
M is the physics abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A tenor, nicely positioned, talks about skipping Mass but insists he meant well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favourably placed' is the idiom 'well in', as in being well in with the boss; 'spoke' is a verb here, not part of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting from the best of motives is a fair gloss of meaning well, whatever the outcome.

clue.text: Put down tip from firefighter

definitions.meaning: to disparage or discourage an idea
literal advice a firefighter might give on dousing a blaze

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark set beside a piece of advice from a fireman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be discouraging about a plan; literally it is how you put out a fire.

clue.text: Digital marker little bird mentioned on phone?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of the next
mentioned means the word for a young bird is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a cygnet is a young swan
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A cryptic question about some marker for a little bird that is talked about on the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means worn on a finger (a digit), not electronic; the seal on the ring marks wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal ring worn on a finger was pressed into wax to mark documents.

clue.text: Routine year for adult in exotic capital

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and altered, so the letters are rearranged
year for adult says Y takes the place of A

parts.note: taken as written
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A year's routine for a grown-up living in some exotic capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping one A of CAPITAL for Y gives CYPITAL or CAPITYL, which 'exotic' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective describes what is usual or standard, the ordinary run of things.

clue.text: See 19
An edition of Ancient & Modern?

parts.note: historical means belonging to the past, ancient
novel means new, modern

explanation.surface: Hymns Ancient & Modern is a famous Anglican hymnbook, so the clue seems to ask about a printing of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ? marks the whimsy: a book that is both old (its setting) and new (its form) is an edition of 'ancient and modern'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiction set in a past era is both a period piece and a new-made book, a printed edition.

clue.text: King's noted lodging — building AKA brothel there

indicators.note: building suggests construction from parts, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: The King's famous lodgings, a building also known as a brothel.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley, and 'noted' means set to music: his 1956 hit song.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis, the King of rock and roll, sang about this lonely hotel in a famous song.

clue.text: Centre back in attack last to display violence

indicators.note: the reversed core goes inside the word for an attack

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

indicators.note: back tells us the word for centre is read backwards

parts.note: the core is the centre of something

indicators.note: last to points at the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A footballer, the centre back, in attacking position at last displays violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre back' is a football defender in the surface; here CORE backwards gives EROC, set in FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferocity is fierce savagery, a near synonym of violence.

clue.text: Got up in Paris, enceinte

indicators.note: in says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman (enceinte, French) rose to her feet in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Got up and having risen both describe standing or rising from bed.

clue.text: State prosecutor's lost new coinage

indicators.note: lost says the prosecutor's letters are taken away from the state

parts.note: Florida is a US state
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor; 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A state prosecutor has lost a new piece of legislation or money.
explanation.walkthrough: The florin was a former British two-shilling coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage is a piece of currency; the florin was one such coin.

clue.text: Like child making busy mum irate?

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Is behaving like a child what makes a busy mother cross?
explanation.definitionFit: Childlike behaviour is what we call juvenile or not grown up.

clue.text: Our nation oddly omitted to, in the past

indicators.note: oddly omitted drops the first, third, fifth letters and so on, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Our nation strangely left something out, historically.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic preposition meaning to, as in biblical English.

clue.text: Record answer given by councillor entering race

indicators.note: entering says the next pieces go inside the word for race

parts.note: a tribe is a people, a race

indicators.note: given by sets the second piece alongside the first

explanation.surface: An election report: a councillor answers as he enters the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcribe is to write down or record in writing.

clue.text: Good feed making Spooner's horse kick up a fuss

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
to squeal is to complain loudly

explanation.surface: A satisfying meal makes a horse protest noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A full, nourishing meal is a good feed in informal speech.

clue.text: Yet again take in post, including bill

indicators.note: including says one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to remit money is to send it, as by post
a bill is a poster, an advertisement, AD

explanation.surface: Taking something in again by post, along with a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit is to let someone in again after leaving.

clue.text: Dog runs after bait, nipping child

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the rest
nipping means grabbing with the teeth, so the bait holds the child

parts.note: a lure is a bait
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dog chasing after bait snaps at a child.
explanation.walkthrough: A lurcher is a British crossbred hunting dog, usually part greyhound.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a breed type of hunting dog.

clue.text: Like fox consuming bird without pity?

indicators.note: consuming says the bird is eaten up inside the other word

parts.note: a fox is proverbially sly
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A fox eats a bird mercilessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting harshly and severely is acting without pity.

clue.text: Mad Hatter's rig is more respectable

indicators.note: Mad signals the letters are scrambled, a nod to Alice's tea party

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter's outfit is more respectable than you'd expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight in the comparative means more conventional and upright, more respectable.

clue.text: Mark's successor fighting Mark with little ardour

parts.note: Luke's Gospel follows Mark's in the New Testament
war is fighting
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Mark's successor took up fighting Mark, but without much passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid enthusiasm, half-hearted, as lacking warmth or ardour.

clue.text: Leading light from Staffs turned traitor

parts.note: poles are staffs

indicators.note: turned says the word for traitor is turned round

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: A leading figure from Staffordshire (Staffs) became a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staffs' looks like the county abbreviation but is plural staffs, poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Star guides navigators, literally a light that leads.

clue.text: Low digits from zero in ascending series

indicators.note: the zero is set inside the reversed series
ascending in a down clue means the word for series reads upward

parts.note: a set is a series
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A low-numbers maths puzzle: counting up from zero in a series.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are fingers and toes; the ones down low are on the feet.

clue.text: Farm's latest ducks frighten child's animal

indicators.note: latest points at the final letter of the word

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O
to cow is to intimidate

explanation.surface: The farm's newest ducks scare the child's pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Children call a cow by this nursery word.

clue.text: Prior to support leader in Eucharist

parts.note: to be for something is to support it

indicators.note: leader in picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Before backing the leader in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior to means earlier than, a direct synonym of the preposition.

clue.text: Go north before journalist's prepared to rise

indicators.note: before places the north letter ahead of the journalist

parts.note: to go is to leave
ED is an editor, a journalist; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Head north before the journalist is ready to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' is bread rising: yeast leavens dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough with yeast added is ready to swell up in baking.
